scope: Actual Chromium controls/canvas/workers with simulated localStorage and captured download blobs. Not a hosted service-worker or file-origin persistence test.

results.name: Bottom-ground preset assigns one face and auto-fills without inventing pin nets or undo steps
Top-power dropdown creates a separate named net and honestly reports no attached copper
Through-hole lead accepts a direct plane attachment without an unnecessary via
Opposite-face SMT lead previews then commits an actual trace and via
Discarding an attachment leaves the native board unchanged
One undo or redo handles net assignment, short trace, via and plane state together
Inspector pin action supports keyboard-based plane attachment
Two picked leads connect in one checked batch rather than merging every net
Pad context menu exposes the same explicit plane workflow
A conflicting assigned pin is rejected without a net merge or partial copper
Cancelling the real connection worker adds no proposed copper
A worker proposal cannot overwrite a newer board revision
Board resize refollows and refills the plane without scaling components
Ground preset preserves existing manual copper zones
Auto-refill can be disabled; stale fabrication is blocked until a manual refill
Changing plane assignment requires confirmation and retains existing lead nets
Connections report exposes real disconnected plane islands, not just matching net names
Hide-fill and face-view controls do not alter manufacturing copper
Schema-3 backup and actual file-input import retain planes and verified attachments
Per-face thermal settings persist and trigger a new fill
Screenshots show real plane preview, accepted 3D board and copper-face views
Plane assignment controls remain reachable on a narrow screen
No external runtime requests or uncaught exceptions in plane workflows
